summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a male with a history of dilated cardiomyopathy, systolic heart failure (EF 35%), type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and chronic kidney disease, was admitted for palpitations and shortness of breath after stopping his heart medications due to financial constraints. He reported sleeping upright due to breathing difficulty, and initial evaluation revealed mild pulmonary edema and elevated BNP, consistent with acute on chronic heart failure exacerbation. ICD interrogation showed NSVT but no shock delivery. Symptoms improved with re-initiation of metoprolol and diuresis using torsemide, later transitioned to furosemide for cost reasons. His condition stabilized with improved respiratory status and weight reduction. Social work assisted with a temporary medication supply, and he was discharged home with instructions to monitor weight, continue all cardiac medications, and follow up for sleep apnea evaluation due to reported snoring.
problems: Acute on chronic systolic heart failure
Diabetes with neurological manifestations, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
Personal history of noncompliance with medical treatment, presenting hazards to health
Automatic implantable cardiac defibrillator in situ
